title: Entry Requirements
text: Rival! What have you gone and found this time? And so, we headed off to the stalactite cave on Cal Mira Island, the one that had been turned into a tourist spot. Once inside, we found a section where something like a spherical spatial distortion had formed.
“That’s the thing you can spot wherever there’s an active boss around, right?”
“Yeah. I remember seeing one before.”
“Indeed.”
“So there’s one on this island too, huh… If this is connected to that event, then…”
Itsuki set a catalyst down in front of the sphere with a light tap, and the distortion swelled dramatically.
“Huh… feels like an entrance just opened up.”
“I had a feeling this might be it. It’s probably the gateway to that content. I’d have preferred to avoid it if at all possible, but it looks like we don’t have a choice.”
“There’s no other lead to go on. Guess we push through it.”
Ren and Itsuki said this with matching sighs. Since no other clues had turned up, challenging it seemed like the only sensible option.
“This is that thing everyone was talking about, right? The hardcore completionist stuff.”
“Yes. There’s no other lead, so let’s go in all at once and investigate. Even in these forms, I’m sure we can manage. Besides, everyone else is here too.”
“It’s a gamble, sure, but better than doing nothing.”
“Let us proceed!”
“Let us proceed indeed!”
“Fweeeh…”

And so we approached the distorted sphere. With a whoomph, it shifted shape into something like a gate. Just as we tried to step through, there was a loud thunk. Yuki-chan stood there pressing a hand to her forehead, as if she’d just walked straight into a wall.
“What is this? I can’t get through!”
Kurotarou brought his wing up to the gate, and it pressed flat against something, as though there were an invisible barrier there.
“This is…”
Riska and Rafuemon likewise placed their hands against the wall. Something rippled outward, repelling them, like ripples on water.
“Let Rival check this out, nano.”
Rival pressed a hand to the wall and began chanting a spell.

“Nano… this is an incredibly sturdy barrier, nano. What’s more, it’s being generated from the inflowing activation energy, so even if you break it, it instantly regenerates—and it has a repelling property besides, nano.”
“What a troublesome thing…”
“So our guess was wrong, huh.”
We climbed down from our mounts to try reaching the wall ourselves. And then, my hand passed straight through it.
“Eh?”
Father, Itsuki, and Ren all cried out in surprise at the same moment.
“Ahh… could it be? The entry requirement… might just be our current state.”
“…It would seem so.”
“Somehow, I can tell this was all set up deliberately.”
“In other words, this is a dungeon only heroes can enter.”
Now, of all times, Yuki-chan and the others being unable to participate was quite the predicament indeed.
“Even so, if only we can challenge it, then there’s nothing to do but go.”
“Kuuuh! How frustrating, this is! Motoyasu-sama!”
“Fear not, Yuki-chan! A dungeon of this caliber isn’t even worth troubling your hands over! I’ll leave the rest in your care while I’m away!”
“Understood, Motoyasu-sama!”
I offered words to the frustrated Yuki-chan. Surely, whatever might happen, Yuki-chan and the others could handle things in our stead.
“Itsuki-samaaa…”
“Itsuki-kun…”
Riska and Rafuemon called out to Itsuki with worried voices.

“Please, don’t worry so much. In the first place, this all started because I tried casting a certain spell. I still haven’t pinned down the exact cause, but there’s nothing to do now but see it through.”
Itsuki placed a hand on his chest, answering Riska and the others as if to say, rest easy and wait. Meanwhile, Ren climbed down from Kurotarou and turned around.
“Well then, I’m off.”
“Go get ’em, Ren!”
“Kurotarou…”
“Go, and come back a loner again once you’re back to normal!”
Ren’s eyes slowly filled with exasperation.
“Well, whatever… Sakura-chan, Melty-chan, Gaelion-chan, I’m counting on you three if anything comes up.”
“Okaaay~”
“Yes. Leave the command in case of emergency to Melty.”
“Gaelion will look into various things, nano.”
Father, too, finished his farewells to Sakura-chan and the others.
“By the way, Itsuki, with this kind of event, isn’t there usually something where clearing dungeons on the surrounding islands removes obstacles in the main dungeon?”
“It’s possible, but let’s worry about that once we actually run into such an obstacle.”
“Fair enough. Well then, off we go.”
And so, we stepped into the dungeon’s entrance.
Once inside, the dungeon turned out to look like an ordinary cave. The four of us heroes pressed onward. Before long, we came upon a door.
“Well, let’s keep moving… oof, huh? It won’t open?”
“Er, if I recall the game’s settings correctly, you’re supposed to take the lantern hanging here to proceed.”
Itsuki reached for a lantern hanging on the wall, positioned at just the right height for our current statures. With a rumbling groan, the door creaked open.
“Huh… apparently this lantern’s called the Lantern of Departure.”
“Seems that way. If I remember the setting correctly, the objective is to light a bonfire stand located on a certain floor using this lantern’s flame.”
“Ah, well, Naofumi, why don’t you hold onto it for now? You’ve got a free hand, don’t you?”
“Got it. As for formation, I guess I’ll take the front.”
Father took the lantern from Itsuki and stepped ahead of the rest of us. Ren followed next, then me, with Itsuki bringing up the rear.
“Itsuki and Ren both seem to remember this place—so what kind of dungeon was this back in the game days, anyway?”

“It’s an endgame-style random dungeon. A hundred floors deep, where you defeat monsters and search for stairs down to the next level. Unfortunately, it’s not something meant to be tackled in Filolial form.”
“Same goes for me.”
Since Ren and I both came from the online game group, our understanding of it matched up fairly well.
“Is that so? What about you, Itsuki?”
“The mechanics themselves are the same. It was purely a completionist-type event, though—no achievements or rewards attached, so you’d only bother with it if you actually enjoyed that sort of thing.”
“So it’s not a very rewarding event, huh. If we go by game knowledge and reach the bottom floor only to find nothing there, that’d be a real waste of effort.”
At Father’s words, Itsuki and Ren both smiled as if to say there was nothing to worry about.
“Naofumi, didn’t Motoyasu and Gaelion say our game knowledge was a trap set by the mastermind?”

“If that trap-knowledge says this content isn’t worth doing, then conversely, it might actually be quite rewarding. To begin with, we never knew players could end up in a state like this—so perhaps the clear reward is something considerably valuable.”

“Ahh… so the more game knowledge a hero has, the more likely they’d dismiss it as pointless and skip it—meaning there might be some real benefit hidden here. The problem is our current state, though…”
That much was certainly true. First and foremost, priority had to be returning to our original forms.
“For the time being, why don’t we think about what it means that we ended up in these forms? To begin with, why exactly are there four types of Filolial?”
“You’re thinking about that now? Oh—looks like a monster’s shown up.”
A Violet Blob came bouncing toward us.
“Well now, let’s see how tough it is.”
Itsuki fired a preemptive shot with his gun, and the Violet Blob vanished in an instant.
“Hm… doesn’t seem all that different in strength from outside.”
“Glad it’s not like we’ve been weakened back down to level one or something.”
“That possibility is frightening to imagine. In that case, we’d likely end up with zero experience gained at all, due to conflict between us as fellow Legendary Weapon wielders.”
“If anything, in that scenario, going in solo would’ve been the smarter move.”
“Then I’d be completely useless…”

Indeed, Father couldn’t attack in this form. In that case, he’d have to commit entirely to fleeing, or think of some other approach. …? I feel like I’m half-remembering something about this, but perhaps it’s just my imagination.
